answers.answer: Layoffs are triggered when it is necessary to decrease the number of teachers. Teachers are laid off in inverse order of seniority within their classification (with equal seniority resolved by lottery). Seniority is based on length of actual service in the district, categorized by classification (elementary; secondary by subject matter; special subject by specialty; middle school by grade/subject, with crossover rules if teaching 50%+ time in the other classification). A displaced teacher may add years in a displaced classification to seniority in a new classification. Seniority lists are established by the Administration by February 1 of each year for non-continuing contract employees, revised every twelve months, transmitted to the Association, and remain unchanged during military and maternity leave. Seniority is broken by discharge, voluntary quit, failure to respond to a recall notice, or remaining on lay-off for more than twenty-four (24) months. Laid-off teachers must be notified of layoff in writing. Recall notices are sent by registered or certified mail, and teachers have ten (10) calendar days to respond or are deemed to have refused. Laid-off teachers must notify the Superintendent in writing prior to the first day for students to claim first refusal for substitute teaching. Accepting a less than full-time position forfeits recall rights for the remainder of the academic year, but the teacher remains on the recall list for the next school year. Laid-off teachers remain on a recall list for 24 months unless they waive recall rights, resign, fail to accept recall, or fail to report within 30 days. No new teachers may be hired while certified laid-off teachers are available. Laid-off teachers are not prevented from securing other employment during the lay-off period.
